screens.name: Header account entry (Account & Lists flyout) and sign-in prompts
screens.url_pattern: Global nav on every page (#nav-link-accountList, flyout #nav-flyout-accountList). Rebuild: shared header component.
screens.purpose: The main way into sign in, create account and account pages from any page. It also shows who is signed in.
screens.layout: Desktop: right side of the dark nav bar, after 'Deliver to' and the language flag. A two-line link: 'Hello, sign in' (12px) above 'Account & Lists' (14px bold) with a small caret. Then 'Returns & Orders', then Cart. Hovering opens a white flyout (~480px) anchored under the link and dims the page. Signed-out flyout, top to bottom: centered yellow 'Sign in' button (~220px), the line 'New customer? Start here.', a hairline, then two columns 'Your Lists' | 'Your Account'. Signed-in flyout: a gray strip at the top reading 'Who is shopping? Select a profile.' with 'Manage Profiles ›', the same two columns, and 'Switch Accounts' and 'Sign Out' at the end of 'Your Account'. On the first signed-out desktop visit, a small tooltip under the link offers a 'Sign in' button and 'New customer? Start here.' and closes on its own. The signed-out homepage also has a card 'Sign in for the best experience' with a yellow 'Sign in securely' button. Mobile web: no flyout. The top bar shows 'Sign in ›' or 'Mikey ›' with a person icon next to the cart; tapping goes straight to sign in or to Your Account. The hamburger menu ends with 'Your Account' and 'Sign in' or 'Sign Out'.
elements: Flyout: 'New customer? Start here.' ('Start here.' is the link, to /ap/register)
Flyout column 'Your Lists': 'Create a List', 'Find a List or Registry'

Flyout column 'Your Account': 'Account', 'Orders', 'Recommendations', 'Browsing History', 'Watchlist', 'Video Purchases & Rentals', 'Kindle Unlimited', 'Content & Devices', 'Subscribe & Save Items', 'Memberships & Subscriptions', 'Music Library'
Signed-in only: 'Who is shopping? Select a profile.' strip, 'Manage Profiles ›', 'Switch Accounts', 'Sign Out'
'Returns & Orders' two-line link next to Account & Lists (goes to sign in if signed out)
Homepage card: 'Sign in for the best experience' + 'Sign in securely'
states: Signed out: 'Hello, sign in'. The flyout has the Sign in button and the Start here link
Signed in: 'Hello, Mikey' (first name only). The flyout has profiles, Switch Accounts and Sign Out
Recognized but session expired ('Keep me signed in' cookie is present): still greets by name, but orders, account and checkout pages ask for the password again
First visit signed out: the auto tooltip appears once, then closes
interactions: Hover opens the flyout after a short delay (~200-300ms) and dims the page; moving the mouse away closes it
Clicking 'Account & Lists' goes to /gp/css/homepage.html, or to sign in with a return path to that page when signed out
'Sign in' in the flyout returns to the current page after sign in (openid.return_to = current URL)
'Sign Out' signs out right away with no confirmation and lands on the sign-in page
Keyboard: the flyout is hard to reach (a known weakness). A 'skip' style focus path is missing
microcopy: Who is shopping? Select a profile.
Sign in for the best experience

screens.name: Sign in, step 1: identifier (unified 'Sign in or create account')
screens.url_pattern: /ap/signin?openid.return_to=<encoded URL>&openid.assoc_handle=usflex&openid.mode=checkid_setup&openid.ns=http://specs.openid.net/auth/2.0 (plus openid.pape.max_auth_age=0 when fresh auth is forced). The new-customer branch continues under /ax/claim/... (memory). Rebuild: /signin?next=/checkout
screens.purpose: A single email-first entry. Amazon checks whether the email or mobile number belongs to an account and sends the user to the password step or the create-account branch.
screens.layout: Desktop: plain white page. The Amazon smile logo (~103px wide) is centered at the top and links home. Below it, a card ~350px wide with a 1px #DDD border, 8px radius and ~20-26px padding: H1 'Sign in or create account' (28px, regular weight); bold label 'Enter mobile number or email'; a full-width input ~31px tall, autofocused; a full-width yellow rounded 'Continue' button; 12px legal line; a 'Need help?' expander with a caret. Then a hairline and 'Buying for work?' (bold) with the link 'Shop on Amazon Business'. Below the card: a gradient hairline, centered small links 'Conditions of Use', 'Privacy Notice', 'Help', and '© 1996-2026, Amazon.com, Inc. or its affiliates'. Legacy variant still seen from some entry points: H1 'Sign in', label 'Email or mobile phone number', 'Continue', legal line, 'Need help?', then a divider with centered gray text 'New to Amazon?' and a full-width gray 'Create your Amazon account' button. Mobile web: no card border, edge-to-edge with ~16px gutters, smaller logo in a light gray top bar, ~44px-tall input and button. The older mobile layout used two radio accordions: 'Create account. New to Amazon?' and 'Sign in. Already a customer?'.
elements: H1 'Sign in or create account' (legacy: 'Sign in')
Label 'Enter mobile number or email' (legacy: 'Email or mobile phone number'). Input type=email/tel hybrid, autocomplete=username
Legal: 'By continuing, you agree to Amazon's Conditions of Use and Privacy Notice.' (both are links)
'Need help?' expander, which reveals 'Forgot your password?' and 'Other issues with Sign-In'
'Buying for work?' + 'Shop on Amazon Business' link
Legacy only: 'New to Amazon?' divider + 'Create your Amazon account' secondary button
Footer links: 'Conditions of Use', 'Privacy Notice', 'Help', copyright line
states: Default: empty field with focus
Returning browser: the field may be prefilled with the remembered email
Empty submit: inline red alert under the field (red ! icon, red field border with a light red glow): 'Enter your mobile number or email' (legacy: 'Enter your email or mobile phone number')
Bad format: 'Invalid email address.' or 'Invalid mobile number' (memory)
Known account: go to the password step (or the passkey prompt if the account has a passkey)
Unknown account, unified flow: go to 'Looks like you're new to Amazon' (the create-account branch)

Unknown account, legacy flow: a red box above the card with heading 'There was a problem' and text 'We cannot find an account with that email address' (for phone: 'We cannot find an account with that mobile number')
Suspected bot or many attempts: a puzzle or CAPTCHA page ('Solve this puzzle to protect your account')
Loading: a full-page form POST, no spinner. The button shows a pressed style only
interactions: Enter key submits
Clicking 'Need help?' toggles the two help links inline (no page change)
The Conditions of Use and Privacy Notice links open help pages in the same tab
return_to is carried through every step, so after success the user lands where they started
microcopy: By continuing, you agree to Amazon's Conditions of Use and Privacy Notice.
Enter your email or mobile phone number
We cannot find an account with that email address

screens.name: Sign in, step 2: password
screens.url_pattern: /ap/signin (POST result, same URL). Rebuild: same page, password field shown inline
screens.purpose: Authenticate a known account with a password, and optionally keep the session long-lived.
screens.layout: Same logo and card. H1 'Sign in'. A row showing the entered identifier (e.g. 'mikey@example.com') with a blue 'Change' link that goes back to step 1. Then a label row: 'Password' on the left and 'Forgot password?' on the right, same line. Password input (autocomplete=current-password). Full-width yellow 'Sign in' button. Then a checkbox 'Keep me signed in.' followed by a blue 'Details' link with a caret. Some variants add a divider and alternatives below: 'Sign in with a passkey' (seen under the password field in 2023) or 'Get an OTP on your phone'. Server errors appear in a separate red-bordered box above the card. Mobile web: the same, full width. 'Show password' checkbox on some mobile variants.
elements: Checkbox 'Keep me signed in.', unchecked by default

Popover heading: '“Keep Me Signed In” Checkbox'. Body: 'Choosing “Keep me signed in” reduces the number of times you're asked to Sign-In on this device.' and 'To keep your account secure, use this option only on your personal devices.'
Optional 'Sign in with a passkey' link
Error box: red triangle icon, heading 'There was a problem', message
states: Empty submit: inline 'Enter your password'

Wrong password: red box above the card, 'There was a problem' / 'Your password is incorrect'. The password field is cleared. Older copy (2016) read 'Your email or password was incorrect. Please try again.'

Repeated failures: an 'Important Message!' box plus an image CAPTCHA under the password ('Enter the characters as they are given in the challenge', with 'Try different image'). The user must re-enter the password and the characters
2SV enabled: goes to the Two-Step Verification OTP page
Account on hold or locked: 'Account on hold temporarily' page asking for a password reset or verification (memory)
Success: optional interstitials ('Add mobile number' / 'Keep hackers out' with 'Not now'; 'Sign in faster with passkeys'), then redirect to return_to
interactions: 'Details' opens a small popover anchored to the link with a close X; clicking outside closes it
'Change' returns to the identifier step with the field prefilled
'Keep me signed in' sets a long-lived cookie. Without it the session ends when the browser closes. Sensitive pages still re-prompt either way
microcopy: Choosing “Keep me signed in” reduces the number of times you're asked to Sign-In on this device.
To keep your account secure, use this option only on your personal devices.

screens.name: New-customer branch in the unified flow ('Looks like you're new to Amazon')
screens.url_pattern: /ax/claim/intent?... then /ax/claim/register (memory). Rebuild: /signin shows this state inline
screens.purpose: When the entered email or mobile has no account, confirm the user wants to create one, then collect the rest of the details with the identifier already filled in.
screens.layout: Card, first screen: H1 'Looks like you're new to Amazon'. Line 'Let's create an account using your email' ('...using your mobile number' for phone), then the identifier in bold with a 'Change' link. Yellow full-width 'Proceed to create an account'. Divider, then 'Already a customer?' and the link 'Sign in with another email or mobile'. Next screen (create account with the identifier locked): 'Your name' (placeholder 'First and last name'), 'Password' (placeholder 'At least 6 characters') with an info line 'Passwords must be at least 6 characters.', 'Re-enter password', a yellow 'Verify email' button, and the legal line 'By creating an account, you agree to Amazon's Conditions of Use and Privacy Notice.' Exact wording of this 2024-25 branch is from memory; medium confidence.
elements: H1 'Looks like you're new to Amazon'
'Let's create an account using your email' + identifier + 'Change'
'Proceed to create an account' yellow button
'Already a customer?' + 'Sign in with another email or mobile'
states: Email identifier: the next step is email OTP
Mobile identifier: the next step is SMS OTP
Validation errors are the same as the Create account form
interactions: 'Change' or 'Sign in with another email or mobile' returns to step 1
microcopy: Looks like you're new to Amazon
Let's create an account using your email
Sign in with another email or mobile

screens.name: Create account form
screens.purpose: Full registration form: name, email or mobile, password.
screens.layout: Desktop: logo; card ~350px: H1 'Create account'; 'Your name' (placeholder 'First and last name'); 'Mobile number or email'; 'Password' (placeholder 'At least 6 characters') with a blue (i) info line 'Passwords must be at least 6 characters.'; 'Re-enter password'; a full-width yellow button, 'Continue' in older versions, now 'Verify email' when the value looks like an email and 'Verify mobile number' for a phone (memory); legal line; hairline; 'Buying for work?' + 'Create a free business account'; 'Already have an account? Sign in ›'. Footer the same as sign in. Mobile web: full width. Instead of 'Re-enter password' there is a 'Show password' checkbox. Label 'Create a password' in some mobile variants.
elements: Input 'Your name' (placeholder 'First and last name', autocomplete=name)
Info hint '(i) Passwords must be at least 6 characters.'
Legal 'By creating an account, you agree to Amazon's Conditions of Use and Privacy Notice.'
'Buying for work?' + 'Create a free business account'
states: Client validation runs on submit. Each failing field gets a red border and an inline message with a red ! icon, and the info hint is swapped for the error
Name empty: 'Enter your name'
Email/mobile empty: 'Enter your email or mobile phone number'
Email/mobile malformed: 'Wrong or Invalid email address or mobile phone number. Please correct and try again.'
Password empty or under 6 characters: 'Minimum 6 characters required'
Re-enter empty: 'Type your password again'
Re-enter mismatch: 'Passwords must match'

Email already used: error box 'Email address already in use'. Text says an account already exists with that email, with a 'Sign in' link and a 'Forgot your password?' link (the help page title confirms the 'E-mail address already in use' error; body wording is memory)
Success: go to the OTP verification step
interactions: Errors clear on the next submit, not while typing (Amazon behavior)
'Sign in ›' goes back to /ap/signin keeping return_to
microcopy: Passwords must be at least 6 characters.
By creating an account, you agree to Amazon's Conditions of Use and Privacy Notice.
Enter your email or mobile phone number
Wrong or Invalid email address or mobile phone number. Please correct and try again.

screens.name: Verify email address (OTP) during sign-up
screens.purpose: Prove ownership of the email before the account is created.
screens.layout: Logo; card: H1 'Verify email address'; body 'To verify your email, we've sent a One Time Password (OTP) to mikey@example.com' with a '(Change)' link; label 'Enter OTP'; numeric input (6 digits, autocomplete=one-time-code); full-width yellow 'Create your Amazon account'; legal line 'By creating an account, you agree to Amazon's Conditions of Use and Privacy Notice.'; link 'Resend OTP' at the bottom. Mobile-number variant: H1 'Verify mobile number', 'A text with a One Time Password (OTP) has been sent to your mobile number: +1 555...'. Sometimes a puzzle step ('Solve this puzzle to protect your account') comes before the OTP is sent.
elements: Body with the masked or full email + '(Change)'
states: Default: code sent. Email subject 'Verify your new Amazon account'. Body: 'To verify your email address, please use the following One Time Password (OTP):' followed by the large 6-digit code, then 'Do not share this OTP with anyone. Amazon takes your account security very seriously...' (memory)
Wrong code: inline 'Invalid OTP. Please check your code and try again.' (memory)
Expired code (~10 min): same invalid message. The user must resend
Resent: a small green or info line saying a new OTP has been sent (memory)
Too many attempts: temporary block, try again later
Success: account created and signed in, redirect to return_to (usually the homepage). An optional 'Add mobile number' interstitial may appear
interactions: 'Resend OTP' sends a new code and invalidates the old one
'(Change)' returns to the create-account form with values kept (except passwords)
microcopy: To verify your email, we've sent a One Time Password (OTP) to

screens.name: Passkey prompts (enrollment interstitial and passkey sign-in)
screens.url_pattern: Interstitial after sign in (/ap/... or /ax/...), setup from Login & security. Rebuild: /account/security/passkey
screens.purpose: Password-free sign in with WebAuthn (Face ID, Touch ID, Windows Hello, PIN).
screens.layout: Enrollment interstitial, a full page (not a modal) shown after a successful password (+OTP) sign-in on a device, never on the homepage: platform icon, title 'Sign in faster with passkeys', body 'Use Face ID, Touch ID, Windows Hello, or your screen lock to sign in. No password required', yellow 'Set up', link 'Not now', and an inline 'Learn more' expander. Clicking 'Set up' opens the OS or browser passkey sheet, then shows a confirmation. In Login & security the 'Passkey' row reads 'Sign in the same way you unlock your device by using your face, fingerprint, or PIN.' with a 'Set up' button; once enrolled it becomes 'Edit', leading to a list of passkeys (device or provider name, created date) with remove. Sign-in: for an account with a passkey, Continue on step 1 triggers the browser passkey sheet (default on mobile). The password path stays available ('Sign in with a passkey' used to appear under the password field).
elements: Body copy naming the platform authenticators
states: Unsupported browser: the prompt is not shown
User cancels the OS sheet: stays on the interstitial or falls back to the password
Passkey failure at sign in: 'We couldn't sign in with a passkey. You can still use your password' (third-party teardown; low confidence)
Shown once per device, stops after being dismissed about twice (teardown)
interactions: 'Set up' calls navigator.credentials.create; 'Not now' continues to return_to
Multiple passkeys are allowed (one per device or provider ecosystem)
microcopy: Use Face ID, Touch ID, Windows Hello, or your screen lock to sign in. No password required

screens.name: Two-Step Verification challenge (sign-in OTP)
screens.purpose: Second factor for accounts with 2SV turned on.
screens.layout: Logo; card: H1 'Two-Step Verification'. Body 'A text with a One Time Password (OTP) has been sent to your phone number ending in 23' or 'For added security, please enter the One Time Password (OTP) generated by your Authenticator App'. 'Enter OTP' input; checkbox 'Don't require OTP on this browser'; yellow 'Sign in'; link 'Didn't receive the OTP?', which expands 'Resend OTP' and other methods (call, backup authenticator). Push-approval variant: 'Approve the notification sent to...' with auto-polling.
elements: 'Don't require OTP on this browser' checkbox
states: Invalid code: 'The One Time Password (OTP) you entered is not valid. Please try again.' (memory)
Lost device: 'Two-Step Verification Recovery' path with ID upload (skip)
interactions: Checking 'Don't require OTP on this browser' marks the device as trusted
microcopy: Don't require OTP on this browser

screens.name: Password assistance (reset)
screens.purpose: Regain access by verifying ownership of the email or phone and setting a new password.
screens.layout: Step 1 card: H1 'Password assistance'; 'Enter the email address or mobile phone number associated with your Amazon account.'; label 'Email or mobile phone number'; yellow 'Continue'. Below the card: bold 'Has your email address or mobile phone number changed?' and 'If you no longer use the e-mail address associated with your Amazon account, you may contact Customer Service for help restoring access to your account.' Step 2 card: H1 'Verification required'; 'To continue, complete this verification step. We've sent an OTP to the email mikey@example.com. Please enter it below to complete verification.'; 'Enter OTP'; yellow 'Continue' (older 'Submit Code'); 'Resend OTP'; option to 'Send OTP by WhatsApp' in some flows. Step 3 card: H1 'Create new password'; 'We'll ask for this password whenever you sign in.'; 'New password' (placeholder 'At least 6 characters') + info 'Passwords must be at least 6 characters.'; 'Password again'; yellow 'Save changes and sign in'. Beneath: 'Secure password tips:' bullets ('Use at least 8 characters, a combination of numbers and letters is best.', 'Do not use the same password you have used with us previously.', 'Do not use dictionary words, your name, e-mail address, mobile phone number or other personal information that can be easily obtained.', 'Do not use the same password for multiple online accounts.').
elements: 'Has your email address or mobile phone number changed?' help block
H1 'Create new password' + 'New password' + 'Password again' + 'Save changes and sign in'
states: Empty: 'Enter your email or mobile phone number'
Unknown: 'There was a problem' / 'We cannot find an account with that email address'
Wrong or expired OTP: invalid OTP inline error
Weak or short password: 'Minimum 6 characters required'
Mismatch: 'Passwords must match'
Reused password: rejected with a message to choose a new one (memory)
Success: signed in, redirected to return_to; a 'Your Amazon password has been changed' style email is sent
interactions: Reached from 'Forgot password?' (step 2 of sign in) or from 'Need help?' > 'Forgot your password?'. The identifier is prefilled when known
The whole flow keeps return_to
microcopy: Enter the email address or mobile phone number associated with your Amazon account.
We'll ask for this password whenever you sign in.

screens.name: Sign out and account switcher
screens.purpose: End the session. Switch between up to several remembered accounts.
screens.layout: No confirmation. 'Sign Out' in the flyout or mobile menu clears the session and redirects to the /ap/signin identifier step, often with the email remembered, rather than the homepage. The cart becomes the device/guest cart. Switch accounts page: H1 'Switch accounts'; a list of account rows (name, email, 'Signed in' badge on the current one); '+ Add account'; 'Manage' mode to remove accounts from the list; 'Sign out' per account.
elements: 'Sign Out' link (flyout bottom-right of 'Your Account' column)
states: After sign out: header shows 'Hello, sign in'; account pages redirect to sign in
Back button after sign out: account pages ask to sign in again
interactions: A single click signs out; the page reloads to sign in

screens.name: Your Account hub
screens.purpose: A card-grid index of everything account-related.
screens.layout: Desktop: centered container ~1000px. H1 'Your Account' (28px). A grid of 3 columns of cards (~320x100px, 1px #D5D9D9 border, 8px radius, 66px line icon on the left, bold 17px title, 14px gray one-line description; light gray background on hover; the whole card is clickable). Below the grid, a hairline, then a 3-column grid of bordered link boxes, each with a bold heading and 5-10 plain text links (the 'link farm'). Mobile web: greeting 'Hello, Mikey' at the top, pill buttons 'Your Orders', 'Buy Again', 'Your Account', 'Your Lists', then grouped list sections with chevron rows (Orders, Account settings, Payments, Communication...).

Card 'Login & security': 'Edit login, name, and mobile number'
Card 'Your Addresses': 'Edit, remove or set default address'

Card 'Your Lists': 'View, modify, and share your lists, or create new ones'

Link boxes (headings): 'Digital content and devices', 'Email alerts, messages, and ads', 'More ways to pay', 'Ordering and shopping preferences', 'Other accounts', 'Shopping programs and rentals', 'Subscriptions', 'Memberships and subscriptions', 'Communication and content', 'Data and Privacy' (incl. 'Request your data', 'Close Your Amazon Account', 'Privacy Notice')
states: Signed out: redirect to /ap/signin with return_to = hub
Signed in: full grid; card order is fixed, not personalized
Server error: Amazon's 'Sorry! Something went wrong on our end' dog page
interactions: Card click navigates (full page). No inline previews such as order counts or default address

screens.name: Login & security
screens.url_pattern: /ax/account/manage?... (older /ap/cnep). Always reached through a forced re-auth (max_auth_age=0). Rebuild: /account/security
screens.purpose: View and edit sign-in identity: name, email, mobile, passkey, password, 2SV.
screens.layout: Desktop: breadcrumb 'Your Account › Login & security'; H1 'Login & security'; a single bordered box (~600px, 8px radius) of rows split by 1px lines. Each row has a bold label and gray value or description on the left, and a small gray bordered 'Edit' button on the right. Rows in order: 'Name' | 'Email' | 'Primary mobile number' (with 'Quickly sign in, easily recover passwords, and receive security notifications with this mobile number.') | 'Passkey' ('Sign in the same way you unlock your device by using your face, fingerprint, or PIN.', button 'Set up') | 'Password' ('********') | '2-step verification' ('Add a layer of security. Require a verification code in addition to your password.', button 'Turn on' or 'Manage') | 'Compromised account?' ('Take steps like changing your password and signing out everywhere.', button 'Start'). Older layout ended with a yellow 'Done' button returning to Your Account. Mobile web: the same rows full width, and the Edit buttons stay on the right.
elements: Row 'Primary mobile number' + value or empty + 'Edit'/'Add'
states: Entry: if not freshly authenticated, shows the sign-in password step first (email shown, 'Password', 'Sign in')
After a successful edit: green alert at the top, 'Success' / 'You have successfully modified your account!' (memory)
No mobile: value empty, button 'Add'
interactions: Each 'Edit' goes to a separate full page (not inline); save returns to this page with the success alert
2SV 'Turn on' goes to '/a/settings/approval' Two-Step Verification (2SV) Settings

screens.name: Login & security edit forms (name, email, mobile, password) and 2SV settings
screens.url_pattern: /ap/cnep?... /ax/account/manage/... (per field); 2SV: /a/settings/approval. Rebuild: inline row editors on /account/security
screens.purpose: Change a single identity attribute with appropriate verification.
screens.layout: All are simple single-card pages with a breadcrumb back to Login & security. CHANGE NAME: H1 'Change your name'; 'If you want to change the name associated with your Amazon customer account, you may do so below. Be sure to click the Save Changes button when you are done.'; label 'New name'; yellow 'Save changes'. CHANGE EMAIL: H1 'Change your email address'; 'Current email address:' + value; 'Enter the new email address you would like to associate with your account below. We will send a One Time Password (OTP) to that address.'; 'New email address'; yellow 'Continue'; then an OTP page ('Enter OTP'), then the password confirmation, then save. Other devices must sign in again. CHANGE MOBILE: H1 'Change mobile number'; country code select 'US +1'; 'Mobile number'; 'Continue'; SMS OTP 'Verify mobile number'. CHANGE PASSWORD: H1 'Change Password'; 'Use the form below to change the password for your Amazon account'; 'Current password'; 'New password' + 'Passwords must be at least 6 characters.'; 'Reenter new password'; yellow 'Save changes'; 'Secure password tips' box. 2SV SETTINGS: H1 'Two-Step Verification (2SV) Settings'; status 'Disabled' + 'Get Started'; Step 1 'Enroll a 2SV authenticator' with the choice 'Phone number' (country, number, 'Send OTP', 'Enter OTP', 'Verify OTP and continue') or 'Authenticator App' (QR code, 'Can't scan the barcode?', 'Enter OTP', 'Verify OTP and continue'); a backup method is required; Step 2 'Almost done...' with 'Don't require OTP on this browser' explanation and 'Got it. Turn on Two-Step Verification'. When enabled: 'Preferred method', 'Backup methods', 'Add new phone or Authenticator App', 'Make default', 'Remove', 'Disable'.
elements: 'Change your email address' + 'Current email address:' + 'New email address' + 'Continue'
'Change Password' + 'Current password' + 'New password' + 'Reenter new password' + 'Save changes'
2SV settings: status, 'Get Started', authenticator enrollment, backup methods
states: Name empty: 'Enter your name'
Email invalid: 'Invalid email address'; email taken: error saying the address is already in use (memory)
Current password wrong: 'There was a problem' / 'Your password is incorrect'
New password short: 'Minimum 6 characters required'; mismatch: 'Passwords must match'
Success: return to Login & security with the green success alert
interactions: Save posts the form and redirects; 'Cancel' is the breadcrumb or back

screens.name: Your Addresses
screens.purpose: Address book used by checkout: add, edit, remove, set the default shipping address.
screens.layout: Desktop: container ~1000px; breadcrumb 'Your Account › Your Addresses'; H1 'Your Addresses'. A grid of fixed-size tiles (~320x290px, 3 per row, 1px #D5D9D9 border, 8px radius). Tile 1 is always 'Add address': a 2px dashed gray border, a large gray '+' and bold 'Add address' centered. The default address tile comes second, with a header strip reading 'Default:' followed by a small Amazon logo. Tile body: bold full name, address line 1, line 2, 'CITY, ST 12345-6789', 'United States', 'Phone number: 555-555-0123', and a link 'Add delivery instructions' (or the saved instructions summary). Tile footer, blue links separated by pipes: 'Edit | Remove | Set as Default'. The default tile has only 'Edit | Remove'. Mobile web: an 'Add a new address' row with a chevron at the top, then full-width stacked cards with gray buttons 'Edit', 'Remove', 'Set as Default' in a row.
elements: Address tile: name, lines, city/state/ZIP, country, 'Phone number:'
states: Empty (new account): only the 'Add address' tile
One address: it is not automatically default on every path; the default strip shows when set
After add: green alert at the top, 'Address saved' (memory)
After set default: tile moves to position 2 with the 'Default:' strip; alert 'Default address changed' (memory)
After remove: alert 'Address removed' (memory). Pending orders to that address are unaffected
Signed out: redirect to sign in with return_to
interactions: 'Remove' opens a modal 'Confirm removal' showing the address summary with a yellow 'Yes' and a 'No' (verified: 'Yes')
'Set as Default' is a one-click POST and page reload
'Edit' goes to the edit form prefilled

flows.name: Checkout auth gate with return to origin (returning customer)
steps: Signed-out shopper has items in the device (guest) cart and clicks 'Proceed to checkout'
Server responds 302 to /ap/signin?openid.return_to=<URL-encoded checkout URL> (only same-origin return targets allowed)
Identifier step: types email, presses 'Continue' (or Enter)
Account found: password step shows the email + 'Change'; types password; optionally ticks 'Keep me signed in.'; clicks 'Sign in'
If 2SV is on: 'Two-Step Verification' page, 'Enter OTP', 'Sign in'
Optional interstitials: 'Add mobile number' ('Not now') or 'Sign in faster with passkeys' ('Not now')
Guest cart lines merge into the account cart (same item: quantities combined)
Redirect to return_to: checkout opens with the default address and default payment preselected; with no saved address, the address form is shown first

Same gate is used for: 'Returns & Orders', 'Account & Lists' click, 'Add to List', 'Create a List', 'Write a customer review', Your Addresses / Payments / Messages / Prime pages. Cart and browsing history work signed out

priorities.feature: Email-first sign in (identifier step, then inline password step) with Amazon error copy ('Enter your email or mobile phone number', 'We cannot find an account with that email address', 'Your password is incorrect')
priorities.why: Gate to checkout and orders. Without it the shopping loop cannot be completed as a real account.

priorities.feature: Create account (name, email, password min 6) with inline validation, unique email, argon2/bcrypt hashing
priorities.why: New judges have no account; sign-up must take under 20 seconds and never fail silently.

priorities.feature: Session cookie (httpOnly, SameSite=Lax) + 'Keep me signed in' (browser session vs 30-day)
priorities.why: Core auth plumbing; the checkbox is one line of expiry logic.

priorities.feature: Sign out
priorities.why: Expected, trivial, needed to demo signed-out vs signed-in states.

priorities.feature: Auth gate + return-to-origin (next= param, same-origin only) for checkout, orders, account pages, add-to-list
priorities.why: Amazon's key efficiency: sign in drops you back exactly where you were. Open-redirect-safe validation is a security must.

priorities.feature: Guest cart merge into account cart on sign-in/sign-up
priorities.why: Losing the cart at the sign-in wall breaks the core loop.

priorities.feature: Header 'Hello, sign in / Hello, {name}' + 'Account & Lists' flyout (signed-in and signed-out states)
priorities.why: Primary entry point judges will click first; cheap.

priorities.feature: Your Addresses: list tiles, Add address tile, add/edit form with required-field validation, Remove with confirm, Set as Default
priorities.why: Checkout needs a shipping address; the same form component serves checkout and the address book.

priorities.feature: Your Account hub (card grid limited to built features: Orders, Login & security, Addresses, Payments, Lists, Browsing history)
priorities.why: Cheap static grid; makes the account area feel complete. Skip the 40-link farm.

priorities.feature: Login & security: edit name, email (no OTP), password (requires current password)
priorities.why: Strongly expected; simple CRUD on the user row.

priorities.feature: Your Payments wallet: add card (store brand, last4, expiry, name only; demo/test numbers), set default, remove with confirm, expired flag
priorities.why: Makes checkout payment selection real without PCI scope. Never store PAN/CVV.

priorities.feature: Browsing history page: record PDP views, grid, Remove from view, Remove all, on/off toggle
priorities.why: Cheap (one table plus an insert on PDP view) and also powers homepage 'Keep shopping for' rows.

priorities.feature: Sign-in rate limiting / lockout message ('Too many attempts. Try again in a few minutes.')
priorities.why: Minimal abuse protection for a public deploy; replaces Amazon's CAPTCHA.

priorities.feature: Show-password toggle and correct autocomplete attributes on all auth/address/card fields
priorities.why: A few attributes give big UX and accessibility gains, and password managers work out of the box.

priorities.feature: Password assistance (reset via emailed code or link)
priorities.why: Needs a transactional email provider and token table. Link 'Forgot password?' must still exist; implement if email is wired.

priorities.feature: Email OTP verification at sign-up ('Verify email address', 'Enter OTP', 'Resend OTP')
priorities.why: Adds friction and an email dependency for a demo. Build the table and screen only if email sending is already in place.

priorities.feature: Passkey sign-in and enrollment (WebAuthn via a small library)
priorities.why: Impressive and on-trend (Amazon's default on mobile) but browser edge cases eat time. Do it after the loop is solid.

priorities.feature: Your Messages: auto-generated 'Order placed' / 'Shipped' messages list + detail
priorities.why: Easy once orders exist; low judge value vs. core loop.

priorities.feature: Prime membership page (static: plan, next payment date, benefits, disabled 'End membership')
priorities.why: Visual completeness only; no billing logic.

priorities.feature: Delivery instructions on addresses; ZIP to city/state autofill; address suggestion modal
priorities.why: Nice polish; USPS verification API is out of scope, static ZIP lookup is optional.

priorities.feature: Sign out of all devices / 'Compromised account?' and Close your account
priorities.why: Delete sessions by user id is one query; good hygiene if time allows.

priorities.feature: Mobile-number accounts and SMS OTP sign-in
priorities.why: Requires SMS provider, cost, and toll-fraud exposure; email covers the demo.

priorities.feature: 2-Step Verification (authenticator app, SMS, backup methods, trusted browsers)
priorities.why: High effort (TOTP enrollment, backup method rules, recovery) with little visible value in a 24h judged demo.

priorities.feature: CAPTCHA / 'Solve this puzzle' / 'Important Message!' challenges
priorities.why: No bot pressure at demo scale; rate limiting is sufficient and keeps the flow fast.

priorities.feature: Amazon Business sign-up, Amazon Family/Household, 'Who is shopping?' profiles, Switch Accounts

priorities.feature: Gift cards balance/redeem, checking accounts, Shop with Points, store card, Transactions tab

priorities.feature: Prime sign-up, billing and cancellation retention flow
priorities.why: Subscription billing and legal copy; a static page is enough.

priorities.feature: Archived orders
priorities.why: Belongs to the Orders surface; rarely used.

priorities.why: Complexity for little demo value; requiring current password on password change covers the risky edit.

priorities.feature: Real card storage / real payment processing
priorities.why: PCI scope. Store only brand, last4, expiry, and simulate authorization.

better_than_original: One page instead of 2-4 full page loads: the password field (or the 'new here' name field) slides in under the email after 'Continue', with the email still visible and editable. It keeps Amazon's email-first branching but has no reloads and no lost typing.
Drop 'Re-enter password' and add an eye toggle ('Show'). Show a live check of the length rule ('6+ characters') beside the field instead of an error that only appears on submit.

Validate each field on blur and clear errors while the user types. Link each error with aria-describedby and aria-invalid, move focus to the first invalid field, and announce a summary in an aria-live region. Amazon only validates on submit, and its ! icon messages are visual-first.

Set correct autocomplete tokens everywhere: username, current-password, new-password, name, tel, street-address, address-line1/2, address-level1/2, postal-code, cc-number, cc-name, cc-exp, one-time-code. Password managers and browser autofill then fill sign-in, addresses and cards in one tap.

Replace the 'Keep me signed in' Details popover with one short line of helper text under the checkbox ('Stay signed in on this device for 30 days. Don't use on shared computers.'). The same information with no hidden click.
Carry the pending action through sign-in, not just the page: after signing in from 'Add to List' or 'Buy Now', finish that action automatically and show a toast.
Merge the guest cart visibly: after sign-in, show a toast such as '2 items from this device were added to your cart' so shoppers never wonder where items went.

Account hub shows only features that work, in three labeled groups: Orders & shopping, Account & security, Addresses & payments. Each card shows live context (e.g. 'Default: 123 Main St', 'Visa •••• 4242 default', '3 orders in transit'). Drop the 40-link farm.
Login & security edits happen in place: the row expands into a form, saves with a toast, and needs no separate page or 'Done' button. Password change still asks for the current password.

Removing an address or card shows 'Removed. Undo' for about 6 seconds instead of a blocking 'Confirm removal' modal (deletion is soft until the toast expires). Keep a real confirm only for irreversible 'Remove all browsing history'.

Address form: ZIP first (it auto-fills City and State from a small static ZIP table) and fewer visible fields. 'Apt, suite' stays optional and collapsed on mobile. Phone hint explains why it's needed. Same component reused at checkout.
Default address and default card always appear first with a clear 'Default' badge. 'Set as default' is a single optimistic click with no page reload.

Wallet on mobile opens as a single list with a detail bottom sheet instead of two panes. Expired cards show 'Expired: update' inline with the expiry editable right there. If a card is used by an open order, explain why it can't be removed before the user tries.
Browsing history groups items by day, uses a real labeled switch ('Browsing history: On') with plain text explaining what turning it off does, and removes items instantly with undo.

Consistent, specific error copy in one voice (e.g. 'No account found for mikey@example.com. Create one?' with an inline 'Create account' button), instead of Amazon's mix of 'There was a problem' boxes and inline alerts.

Accessibility and speed basics Amazon misses on these pages: visible focus rings, keyboard-openable account menu (button with aria-expanded, not hover-only), 44px touch targets, dark-mode tokens, and pages that stay fast because account pages are small server-rendered forms.
